content.content: When the marker state cannot be written after the write half, the invocation reverses the inverse it applied and refuses, naming the cause: undo and redo alike. A recording's recovery applies the before side again; a change-level recovery reverses its crossings. The graph returns to its pre-invocation state and the marker file is left as it was.
content.rationale: S5-save-after-revert (kqqysmxn) orders the write half before the save so a revert cannot take the record of the operation with it, but leaves open what the invocation leaves when the save itself fails. S2-markers-write-fail (xokynzpp) fixes that the failed write refuses, naming the cause, and leaves the file as it was; S2-markers-refusal-site (sprvousp) that the invocation touching the file produces the refusal. Neither says what becomes of the write half already made, and a graph left inverted under a marker state that still says applied cannot be walked back. S5-revert (qxmzpupt) already fixes the remedy — the inverse already made is reversed, the graph returns to its pre-invocation state, and the invocation refuses — so this decision reuses that remedy rather than inventing a second recovery. A recording's recovery re-applies its before side; a creation's or removal's reverses its crossings.
